review_notes:
I read all of Padding.lean (lines 1–120). I also read the related definitions in MatrixMultiplication/Model.lean (matrixInputs, MatrixAlgorithm.cost, eval, Correct) and the simp lemmas eval_mapSource and cost_mapSource in ProgramComposition.lean. I grepped for uses of zeroPadMatrix, padSource, pad_cost_eq and sum_fin_castLE_of_zero across lean/OAI.

The file has two simp lemmas, zeroPadMatrix_castLE and pad_cost_eq. Both have a clean left-hand side that makes the right-hand side smaller, and neither competes with another rule or can loop. pad_cost_eq is stated on `.cost`, which is a plain def and not simp-unfolded, so the rule fires. I found no unwanted expansion.

The non-simp lemmas are padSource_eval, sum_fin_castLE_of_zero and zeroPadMatrix_mul. All are used only through explicit `rw`, `apply` or `exact`. padSource_eval has a lambda left-hand side and zeroPadMatrix_mul has hypothesis-heavy arguments, so neither would make a good simp lemma. Adding simp attributes there would fail the rubric's caution against annotating identities merely because they look simple.

I flagged nothing for the duplicated copies of these declarations in other files (for example RecursiveBlockPrograms.lean and ComplexArithmeticLowerBound.lean). That is duplication, not a simp-interface issue. I couldn't run Lean, so I made no claims about simp behaviour that I haven't derived from the source.
